dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Hello, and welcome to WKU Radio! Today we're talking to Zhibek Akhmetova, a second-year English student. Zhibek, have you always wanted to study English?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Not always! I used to think English was just for businesspeople. But my attitude has completely changed. I've realised it opens every door — science, culture, travel, everything.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Interesting! Have you ever lived or studied abroad?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Not yet, but I've applied for an exchange programme in Edinburgh. I've always dreamed of studying in Scotland. I haven't heard back yet, but I'm hopeful.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Exciting! And what experiences in Kazakhstan have shaped you most? Have you ever done something that really changed your perspective?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Yes! I've volunteered at a children's hospital in Uralsk for two years. I've met so many incredible young people there. It's completely changed how I see life. I've learned that attitude matters more than circumstances.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: That's powerful. Have you ever performed on stage? I know you studied dance.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Yes! I've danced in twelve public performances. The first time was terrifying — I'd never performed in front of more than fifty people before. But now I love it. I've also choreographed three short pieces.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Twelve performances! That's impressive. Has anything ever gone wrong on stage?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Ha! Once the music stopped mid-performance. I'd never experienced anything like that before. But we kept dancing in silence for thirty seconds until it came back on. The audience loved it — they gave us a standing ovation!

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Amazing! What's the most unusual thing you've ever tried?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I've tried making traditional Kazakh clothing from scratch. It took six months. I've worn it at Nauryz twice now. People always ask me where I bought it — I love telling them I made it myself!

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Wonderful. One last question — what's something you've never done but really want to try?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I've never seen the Northern Lights. That's my number one dream experience. I haven't saved enough money yet, but it's top of my list!
